topics.title: What is an Operating System? (Definitions & Roles)

questions.prompt: What is the role of an operating system?

options.label: A
options.text: To manage hardware resources

options.label: B
options.text: Resolves competing requests to ensure resources are used efficiently and fairly

options.label: C
options.text: Manages program execution and safeguards the system against errors and misuse

options.label: D
options.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: The operating system plays multiple essential roles: it acts as a resource allocator (managing and resolving competing hardware requests) and as a control program (preventing errors and improper computer use).

topics.title: Computer System Architecture & the Von Neumann Model

questions.prompt: Which is not part of the Von Neumann architecture?

options.label: A
options.text: Control unit

options.label: B
options.text: Memory

options.label: C
options.text: Arithmetic Logic Unit

options.label: D
options.text: Operating system

questions.explanation: The operating system is system software and not a physical component of the Von Neumann hardware architecture (which consists of the CPU/ALU, Control Unit, Registers, and Memory).

questions.prompt: Which component below is part of the von Neumann architecture?

options.label: A
options.text: Arithmetic Logic Unit or ALU

options.label: B
options.text: Registers including program counter (PC) and instruction register (IR)

options.label: C
options.text: Memory along with cache

options.label: D
options.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: The Von Neumann architecture specifies a Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing an ALU and registers (like the Program Counter and Instruction Register), alongside Memory (and caches).

questions.prompt: Which of the following components is not a part of the Central Processing Unit in the Von Neumann architecture?

options.label: A
options.text: Control unit

options.label: B
options.text: Registers

options.label: C
options.text: Arithmetic Logic Unit

options.label: D
options.text: Main memory

questions.explanation: In the Von Neumann architecture, main memory is connected to the CPU via a system bus but is separate from the execution components inside the CPU core (such as the Control Unit, ALU, and Registers).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a core characteristic of the von Neumann Architecture?

options.label: A
options.text: Instructions and data are stored in separate physical memories

options.label: B
options.text: Instructions and data are stored in the same memory space, accessed by address

options.label: C
options.text: The CPU does not contain an Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU); all computations are done by an external co-processor

options.label: D
options.text: The Program Counter (PC) is stored in external mass storage devices

questions.explanation: Under the Von Neumann design, instructions and data are stored in the same physical memory space and accessed by address.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about interrupts is false?

options.label: A
options.text: Interrupts may be generated by hardware devices

options.label: B
options.text: Interrupts may be generated by software exceptions or traps

options.label: C
options.text: All interrupts are serviced in exactly the same way, with no difference in priority

options.label: D
options.text: Interrupts are handled by the kernel

questions.explanation: Interrupts have different priorities based on their urgency or importance; they are not all handled with the same status.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is not true about interrupt?

options.label: A
options.text: Interrupts are exclusively used by I/O devices to coordinate the actions with CPU(s)

options.label: B
options.text: Interrupts are caused by asynchronous events to require CPU attention

options.label: C
options.text: Interrupts can have different priorities based on their importance

options.label: D
options.text: Each interrupt needs to be handled by an interrupt handler

questions.explanation: Interrupts are not exclusively for I/O devices; software exceptions, division-by-zero errors, system calls (traps), and hardware timers also generate interrupts to require CPU attention.

questions.prompt: Which of the following events does not generate an interrupt?

options.label: A
options.text: An I/O operation completes

options.label: B
options.text: CPU fetches instruction or data from memory

options.label: C
options.text: An arithmetic error occurs

options.label: D
options.text: A timer expires

questions.explanation: Fetching instructions or data from memory is a standard CPU pipeline cycle and does not trigger an interrupt.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements on interrupt is NOT true?

options.label: A
options.text: I/O devices using DMA technique do not generate interrupt

options.label: B
options.text: Interrupt can be generated by software

options.label: C
options.text: CPU checks whether there is an interrupt between the executions of instructions

options.label: D
options.text: All modern computer systems are interrupt-driven

questions.explanation: Devices utilizing Direct Memory Access (DMA) still issue an interrupt to the CPU upon completing the transfer of a block of data.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true about DMA?

options.label: A
options.text: DMA is used for move data for slow devices, while CPU is used for fast devices

options.label: B
options.text: DMA allows data transfer between device and memory with less CPU involvement

options.label: C
options.text: DMA eliminates interrupts completely

options.label: D
options.text: CPU and DMA can't execute concurrently

questions.explanation: DMA lets high-speed I/O devices transfer blocks of data directly to/from main memory with minimal CPU intervention.

questions.prompt:
During DMA transfer, the following four events occur:
1. Disk controller initializes DMA transfer
2. DMA controller sends an interrupt to CPU upon transfer completion
3. Disk controller is informed with transfer addresses and transfer bytes
4. DMA controller carries out transfer between memory and an I/O device

The correct order of execution is ____.
questions.explanation: The process starts by setting up the disk controller with the addresses and sizes (3). The disk controller initializes the hardware transfer (1). The DMA controller carries out the direct block transfer (4). Finally, it signals the CPU with an interrupt upon completion (2).

questions.prompt: Which of the following statement is true about storage hierarchy?

options.label: A
options.text: Registers are slower than main memory

options.label: B
options.text: Main memory is nonvolatile

options.label: C
options.text: Hard-disk drives is smaller than volatile memory

options.label: D
options.text: Main memory is byte addressable

questions.explanation: Main memory is byte addressable and volatile, meaning it loses its state when power is lost.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements about cache is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: In order for cache to work, access must exhibit temporal and spatial locality

options.label: B
options.text: Cache stores a subset of the data in a faster device

options.label: C
options.text: Cache keeps recently accessed data closer to a processor

options.label: D
options.text: Cache improves the utilization of a slower device

questions.explanation: Cache is designed to improve processor access speed (by moving data closer to the CPU) rather than directly optimizing the physical utilization of the underlying slower device.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about the storage system?

options.label: A
options.text: Electrical storage is generally larger and less expensive per byte than mechanical storage

options.label: B
options.text: Temporal locality in caching exploits the tendency of programs to access the same data item over and again within a small time duration

options.label: C
options.text: Non-Uniform Memory Access is a major approach in system design that bypasses the CPU in the data transfer between the I/O device and memory

options.label: D
options.text: In the caching process, recently accessed data items tend to be copied from smaller to larger storage for sufficient storage capacity

questions.explanation: Temporal locality states that if a program accesses an address once, it is highly likely to access the exact same address again shortly.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is not true about secondary storage?

options.label: A
options.text: Mechanical storage like HDD tends to be slower than electrical storage like NVM

options.label: B
options.text: Mechanical storage per unit capacity is cheaper than electricity storage

options.label: C
options.text: Mechanical storage is more reliable than electricity storage

options.label: D
options.text: Mechanical storage usually has larger capacity than electricity storage

questions.explanation: Electrical storage (such as Solid-State NVM) is significantly more reliable than mechanical storage (HDDs) because it contains no moving physical parts.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is NOT true on memory hierarchy?

options.label: A
options.text: Registers run faster than cache

options.label: B
options.text: The hard-disk drives (HDDs) run faster than nonvolatile memory (NVM) devices

options.label: C
options.text: Memory is more expensive per byte than any secondary storage devices

options.label: D
options.text: The capacity of cache is usually much smaller than that of memory

questions.explanation: Nonvolatile Memory (NVM) is solid-state electrical storage and runs significantly faster than mechanical HDDs.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is false about cache?

options.label: A
options.text: The access time of cache is faster than register

options.label: B
options.text: Cache hit ratio means the percentage of content found in cache

options.label: C
options.text: If the information required is not in cache, data will be copied from a lower storage

options.label: D
options.text: Cache will keep recently accessed data items closer to the processor

questions.explanation: Registers reside directly inside the CPU core and execute in a fraction of a nanosecond (typically 0.25–0.5 ns), which is much faster than cache memory (0.5–25 ns).

questions.prompt: What is the fundamental idea of caching? When designing a cache system, is a high cache hit ratio alone enough to guarantee good performance? Explain by considering hit time and miss penalty.
questions.answer:
The fundamental idea is to temporarily copy a subset of frequently accessed data from a slower, larger storage to a faster, smaller storage.

A high cache hit ratio alone is **not** enough to guarantee good performance. Based on the average access time formula:
$$\text{Average Access Time} = (\text{Hit Ratio} \times \text{Hit Time}) + (\text{Miss Ratio} \times \text{Miss Penalty})$$

If the **miss penalty** (miss time) or the **hit time** is exceptionally high, the overall average access time can still be very high despite a high hit ratio. Therefore, hit time and miss penalty must be kept low to achieve high performance.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is not true for a multicore system?

options.label: A
options.text: It consumes significantly less power

options.label: B
options.text: Communication between CPU cores on the same physical chip is faster than CPU cores residing on separate chips

options.label: C
options.text: Each CPU core has its own local cache

options.label: D
options.text: CPU cores on the same chip communicate with each other through a common bus

questions.explanation: On-chip cores typically utilize specialized high-speed on-chip interconnects rather than the slow standard system physical bus to coordinate.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statement is false about multiprocessor systems?

options.label: A
options.text: A multiprocessor system significantly saves power consumption compared to a single-processor system during the same time period

options.label: B
options.text: In a typical symmetric multiprocessor system, the processors usually have their own local cache while sharing the system bus

options.label: C
options.text: Contention for shared resources lowers the expected performance gain from additional processors in multiprocessor systems

options.label: D
options.text: Multiprocessor system can be implemented with a single chip containing multiple computing cores

questions.explanation: Running multiple processors increases physical power draw compared to a single-processor system over the same timeframe.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not one of the advantages of multiprocessor systems compared to single process systems?

options.label: A
options.text: Economy of scale

options.label: B
options.text: Fast on-chip communication

options.label: C
options.text: More stable

options.label: D
options.text: Can share other devices such as I/O devices

questions.explanation: Fast on-chip communication is an advantage unique to multicore architectures (where multiple cores share a physical silicon die) rather than general multi-chip multiprocessor systems.

questions.prompt: What is a potential drawback of a Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) system?

options.label: A
options.text: Enhanced local memory access due to dedicated CPU connections

options.label: B
options.text: Reduced latency for CPU access to remote memory

options.label: C
options.text: Enhanced scalability with the addition of more CPUs

options.label: D
options.text: Higher latency when accessing remote memory across the system interconnect

questions.explanation: In a NUMA architecture, when a processor is forced to fetch data from memory owned by a different, remote node, it must cross the system interconnect, leading to increased latency.

questions.prompt: How do multiprogramming and multitasking complicate the OS design?

options.label: A
options.text: It requires memory management strategy to allocate memory to different processes in an efficient and protected manner

options.label: B
options.text: It requires CPU scheduling mechanism to determine which process to run on a CPU and for how long

options.label: C
options.text: It requires coordination in concurrent operation on I/O devices and CPU

options.label: D
options.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Concurrent execution forces the OS to handle memory allocation/isolation, scheduling algorithms to distribute CPU cycles, and lock/I/O coordination.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an advantage of virtual memory?

options.label: A
options.text: It allows the execution of processes not completely in memory

options.label: B
options.text: It increases the physical memory available

options.label: C
options.text: It improves CPU performance

options.label: D
options.text: It eliminates the need for context switching

questions.explanation: Virtual memory abstracts physical RAM, allowing systems to run programs larger than physical memory or execute programs partially mapped in memory.
